operational.description: Rising costs from increased insured liability claims and legal settlements that exceed standard inflation rates. Most pronounced in the US due to jury sentiment and punitive damages. US liability claims increased 57% over the past decade. Social inflation emerging in UK and Australia. Managed through US liability reserve strengthening and portfolio reduction.
operational.rationale: In 2023, 27 court cases awarded compensation exceeding USD 100 million each, over a third more than in 2022. Emergence of third-party litigation funding increasing legal actions.
operational.mitigation: Significantly reduced market share in liability business exposed to social inflation. Increased liability reserves. Continuously adapts underwriting approach. Swiss Re Institute constructed Social Inflation Index to measure more accurately.

operational.description: Stalling global life expectancy growth since 2010 with ongoing excess mortality post-pandemic. Excess mortality rates higher than expected in key markets. Key drivers: respiratory diseases (COVID-19, influenza), cardiovascular disease, cancer, metabolic illnesses.
operational.rationale: Without control measures like ongoing vaccinations for elderly, excess mortality could remain 2.5-3% above baseline by 2033. Medical progress and improved healthcare services needed for recovery.
operational.mitigation: Continuously monitors mortality and life expectancy trends. Incorporates latest insights into pricing and reserving assumptions. Actively shares knowledge with clients.

operational.description: Insured natural catastrophe losses totalled USD 135 billion in 2024, marking the fifth consecutive year exceeding USD 100 billion. Driven by hurricanes, severe thunderstorms and floods. Urban development and wealth accumulation in disaster-prone areas amplifying loss events.
operational.rationale: USD 53 billion from global thunderstorms (40% of losses), USD 50 billion from hurricanes, 14% from floods in 2024. Second-highest thunderstorm losses on record.
operational.mitigation: Committed to natural catastrophe business with pricing commensurate with risk. Portfolio steering for balance sheet strength. More than 50 dedicated scientists maintaining 200 natural catastrophe models. Active partnerships with governments.

market.description: Global economic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and changing trade conditions creating market volatility. Impact on insurance demand, pricing, and investment returns.
market.rationale: Fed cut rates by 100bps in 2024 while maintaining restrictive stance. ECB reduced rates by 100bps. Higher rate environment benefits long-tail reinsurance businesses.
market.mitigation: Careful assessment of inflation developments. Portfolio adjustments accordingly. High-quality fixed income portfolios as key pillars.

market.description: Economic growth slowing to 2.8% globally in 2024 from 3% in 2023. Advanced economies at 1.8%. China growth slowed to 5.0% from 5.4%. Emerging market growth at 4.2%.
market.rationale: Recession fears faded in 2024. US maintained 2.8% growth with strong consumer fundamentals. Euro area weak at 0.7%. China facing historical weak domestic demand and ailing real estate sector.
market.mitigation: Views economic conditions as generally favourable for insurers. Strong labour markets and steady growth support insurance demand.

regulatory.description: Swiss Ordinance on Climate Disclosures entered into effect in 2024. Swiss Re committed to net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. Climate Transition Plan submitted for voting at AGM 2025.
regulatory.rationale: Regulatory requirement for Climate Transition Plan. Science-based targets informed by SBTi Corporate Net-Zero Standard. Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions covered.
regulatory.mitigation: Developed comprehensive Climate Transition Plan with three pillars: decarbonisation strategy, carbon removal strategy, and transition-enabling activities. Already achieved 50% reduction in carbon intensity of corporate bond and listed equity portfolio relative to 2018 baseline.

regulatory.description: Swiss Re subject to supervision by FINMA as principal regulator. Subject to Swiss Solvency Test (SST) framework. Regular reporting requirements on capital position, liquidity and risks.
regulatory.rationale: SST ratio above 200-250% target range indicates strong compliance. Group SST 2025 report to be filed with FINMA in April 2025.
regulatory.mitigation: Strong capital position. Sound governance and risk management frameworks. Regular reporting and compliance.

cyber.description: Generative AI marks significant step forward for digital transformation but brings new risks. GenAI vulnerable to sophisticated fraud techniques (deepfakes) and heightened liability concerns. Evolving regulatory risks.
cyber.rationale: Careful management and security of AI-enhanced tools critical. Industry-wide adoption of GenAI across claims, distribution and underwriting creating systemic risks.
cyber.mitigation: Swiss Re embracing GenAI's potential by equipping workforce with AI capabilities. Building on strong cloud and data foundations. Responsible AI principles govern all AI efforts. Supporting clients in managing emerging AI-related risks. Life Guide Scout AI-powered assistant augments underwriting.

esg.description: Scientific evidence shows unmitigated climate change will have significant effects on society and economy. Increasing natural catastrophe losses built into risk expectations.
esg.rationale: Fifth consecutive year of insured natural catastrophe losses exceeding USD 100 billion. Economic expansion, inflation, and intensifying climate-related hazards contributing to losses.
esg.mitigation: Swiss Re's business model depends on understanding and pricing climate risk. Committed to achieving net-zero GHG emissions by 2050. Engagement with clients on transition to net-zero economy. Risk transfer products supporting transition.

esg.description: Swiss Re integrates ESG aspects into underwriting (close to 100% of Strategic Asset Allocation), investments, and operations. ESG Risk Framework developed with sector-specific policies.
esg.rationale: ESG Risk Framework revised with updated defence industry sector-specific policy in 2024. Group Sustainability Committee established to strengthen sustainability governance.
esg.mitigation: Comprehensive ESG risk framework. Sustainability considerations integrated into re/insurance decisions. Responsible investing practices. Decarbonising investment portfolio (50% reduction in carbon intensity).

ai_positioning.summary_en: Swiss Re is integrating AI technologies, particularly GenAI, across its operations to enhance productivity and decision-making. The company emphasizes responsible AI governance while supporting clients in managing AI-related risks. Key applications include automated document processing, underwriting support through AI assistants, and enhanced data analysis capabilities.
ai_positioning.summary_fr: Swiss Re intègre les technologies d'IA, notamment l'IA générative, dans l'ensemble de ses opérations pour améliorer la productivité et la prise de décision. L'entreprise met l'accent sur une gouvernance d'IA responsable tout en soutenant les clients dans la gestion des risques liés à l'IA. Les applications clés incluent le traitement automatisé des documents, le soutien à la souscription par des assistants d'IA et les capacités d'analyse de données améliorées.
